mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate trend consistently compresses equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy eases.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS trend is downward (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0 (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a strong labor market, which typically precedes corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 250), the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain restrictive policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as real rates rise.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 250 (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which correlates with stronger corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO trend is upward (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals labor market weakness that typically precedes reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5 (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST and RSAFS growth fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1350 thousand units, it signals strong consumer confidence and positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1350.0 (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).
